critical_code_review_comments: SuperAdminDashboard.js: create-form Ofsted branch (line ~628) uses `value={['early_years','childrens_home','school'].includes(orgForm.service_type) ? orgForm.service_type : 'early_years'}` which is defensive and correct, but the underlying `orgForm.service_type` state is NOT reset when the user switches from NI ('domiciliary') → Ofsted, so the option shown vs. the state stored can be inconsistent for a render cycle. The submit handler (line ~126) does defend against this by re-applying the whitelist, so no bug — but a `useEffect(() => setOrgForm(f=>({...f, service_type: defaultFor(f.jurisdiction)})), [orgForm.jurisdiction])` would be cleaner.

super_admin.py update_org PATCH: if a payload provides `jurisdiction='ofsted'` WITHOUT `service_type`, it correctly 400s. But if the caller ONLY updates the `name` field on an existing england-org, and later switches jurisdiction in a second PATCH without providing service_type, code handles it correctly. rca of the issue: NI rescan bugfix (root cause): review.py::_run_rescan_background was passing `jurisdiction=org_jurisdiction` (plain 'northern_ireland') to _analyze_meeting, but ai.py::analyze_meeting only branches on the effective jurisdiction strings 'northern_ireland_residential' / 'northern_ireland_domiciliary'. The plain 'northern_ireland' string fell through to the England/CQC else-branch, causing all NI rescans to emit CQC content. Fix: build effective_jurisdiction = f'northern_ireland_{org_service_type or "domiciliary"}' (same pattern already used by transcription_pipeline.py) before the analyze_meeting call. Verified in source; end-to-end behaviour test would require re-running an existing NI meeting through rescan which needs OpenAI credits — did not execute (source-level verification is sufficient given the fix is 1 line and mirrors an existing working code path).
